subject: Heatcheck: OKR focus, resource trades & blockers — QBR litmus
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Heatcheck: OKR focus, resource trades & blockers — QBR litmus

Morning all — quick heatcheck ahead of Friday's leadership sync. I summarized where we are against the highest-risk OKRs and the specific asks we need to resolve before the QBR readout. Please skim and flag anything that needs escalated follow-through.

Summary (top risks):
- Model-serving latency (OKR: 99th pct latency <= 180ms) — at risk due to active infra slot shortages and delayed kernel rollout.
- Dedicated capacity onboarding (OKR: Dedicated GA) — on track for GA, but requires 2x infra engineers for a 3-week ramp to hit perf targets.
- Cost-per-token pilot (Optimize infra-led pilot) — metrics look good but needs final QA and canary approval.

Ask checklist (decisions needed this week):
1) Approve temporary resource trade: loan two infra engineers from Platform Reliability (3-week window starting Mon 9/13).
   - Impact: will delay one noncritical backlog item in infra roadmap (INF-4527) by ~4w.
2) Scope trim proposal: for QBR we present the customer-facing deck with the dedicated GA feature set trimmed to exclude "cross-region failover" (defer to Q4) to ensure reliability story is polished.
3) Canary approval for cost-per-token pilot across 10% of traffic (must sign-off by Thu EOD).

Attachments: Q3_OKR_heatmap_v2.xlsx (heatmap + tradeoffs), MCP_action_items.docx (detailed asks per owner). Drive link at top of thread.

Quick notes on each risk:
- Latency: kernel rollout (KR: runtime v1.1) is stable in staging, but production rollout needs the extra infra hands to calibrate instance profiles and KV caching parameters.
- Dedicated: pre-provisioning is waiting on a small procurement SLA (legal already has the doc in review).
- Cost pilot: product_acceptance test 2 shows no quality regressions; need sign-off on fallback policy.

Recommendation: Approve the 2-person trade for 3 weeks (vanessa to nominate), accept the trimmed GA scope for QBR, and greenlight the 10% canary if no objections by end of day Thu.

Thanks — planning to brief execs Friday.

—
Sofia Ivanova
VP, Product & Strategy
Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heatcheck: OKR focus, resource trades & blockers — QBR litmus

Thanks Sofia — quick clarifying questions inline.

> 1) Approve temporary resource trade: loan two infra engineers from Platform Reliability (3-week window starting Mon 9/13).

Can you confirm which two engs we would pull? I want to make sure we aren't introducing a new single-point for oncall coverage. Also: are these full-time allocation or partial (50/50)?

> 2) Scope trim proposal: ... exclude "cross-region failover" (defer to Q4)

Agree with trimming for QBR if we signal a clear plan to customers. Please add a one-slide note in the QBR deck explaining the deferral rationale.

> 3) Canary approval for cost-per-token pilot across 10% of traffic (must sign-off by Thu EOD).

I need the rollback playbook from reliability (who owns rollback and DB cache warmup timeline).

I can be on the quick sync at 11:30 to align.

—Markus
Head of Engineering

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 12:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heatcheck: OKR focus, resource trades & blockers — QBR litmus

Thanks — I can spare two engineers: Lina Park and Arun Mehta. Both have recent experience with kernel rollouts and can prioritize KV cache tuning. I'll coordinate with oncall to ensure no coverage gaps (they'll be 80% on this for the 3 weeks).

Markus — I'll draft the rollback playbook by 4pm and paste it into the Drive folder. High level:
- Canary window: 10:00–14:00 PT; monitor 99th latency, error rate, client-side degradation.
- Rollback trigger: latency > 25% over baseline or >0.5% error spike for two consecutive 5-min windows.
- Fast rollback path: switch traffic routing to prior model variant + clear KV prefixes (takes ~6m).

Sofia — I endorse the scope trim for QBR. I also propose we add a short "customer impact" slide noting the deferral and our mitigation plan.

Attachments: (none in this note)

—Vanessa
Head of Customer Success

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heatcheck: OKR focus, resource trades & blockers — QBR litmus

Thanks team — quick decision summary to close the loop (for the Friday exec briefing):

Decisions made:
- Resource trade approved: Lina Park and Arun Mehta (80% allocation) allocated for 3 weeks starting 9/13. Vanessa to confirm hand-off notes and oncall buffer.
- Scope trim accepted for QBR: cross-region failover deferred to Q4; add customer-impact/mitigation slide (Vanessa + Product).
- Canary approved for 10% traffic contingent on rollout/playbook paste to Drive (Markus + Vanessa to upload by 16:00).

Open items (owners & dates):
- Procurement SLA status (Legal): Kimberly — update by Fri 9/11 EOD.
- Rollback playbook: Vanessa — Drive link + summary by 16:00 today.
- One-slide deferral rationale: Sofia + Vanessa — draft in the shared deck by Thu 18:00.

I've uploaded the updated heatmap and the action-item doc to Drive (Q3_OKR_heatmap_v2.xlsx, MCP_action_items.docx). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Q3_OKR_heatmap_v2.

I'll include this decision list in the Friday exec packet. If anyone has a blocking objection to the resource trade, flag it now — otherwise we'll move forward.

—
Sofia Ivanova
VP, Product & Strategy
Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
